title: Let go, iii
logline: Wednesday. Gully comes in to have something framed for the first time in eleven years: the 2003 pencil rough of himself hanging the sign. Wood mats it. Gully pays. The pins go back in it at the shack anyway.

panels.composition: The shop. GULLY in the door with a soft creased sheet. First time he's ever come in. WOOD's face.

characters.pose: in the door with a sheet

balloons.text: I've been in here. You weren't looking.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a stocky man in a canvas jacket standing in a frame-shop doorway holding a creased sheet of paper, a thin man behind the counter surprised

panels.composition: The sheet: the pencil rough of Gully on the ladder, 2003, pinholes in every corner.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a soft creased pencil sketch of a man on a ladder hanging a sign, with pinholes in every corner

panels.composition: Wood matting it. Precisely. Gully watching him work for the first time.

balloons.text: I only ever saw the other thing.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man precisely matting a small sketch while a stocky man watches him work with new interest

panels.composition: Gully paying. Full price. Wood ringing it. The Owner at the back, the glasses up.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a stocky man paying at a frame-shop register while a thin man rings it up and an older woman watches over her glasses

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: Gully's first time in the shop. 'I only ever saw the other thing.' 'Frame's the same.'
